subject: Renewal planning: GPU top-up options for Orion Health
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@orionhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal planning: GPU sizing ahead of Jan 2027 renewal

Hi Caroline —

Thanks again for the time last week. As we look toward your contract renewal in January, I pulled the last quarter's usage and wanted to flag a potential capacity gap during weekday peak windows. Short summary below and a couple of options to consider:

Key observations (Jul–Sep 2026):
- Sustained 95th-percentile utilization on your dedicated pool during PST business hours (13:00–17:00 ET).
- KV-cache hit rate improvements have lowered per-token cost, but overall request volume grew ~28% vs prior quarter.
- Three production models show longer tail sequences; these drive most of the peak latency and queue buildup.

Options we recommend before renewal to avoid throttling or degraded p99 latency:
1) Staged top-up: +8 A100-equivalent GPUs (burst pool) to cover current peaks; keep usage-based billing for burst.
2) Permanent resize: +5 GPUs to the dedicated pool and convert 3 GPUs of current burst capacity into reserved for a lower unit price.
3) Optimized routing + priority batching: keep current capacity but deploy request-level routing to shift non-latency critical jobs to lower-cost nodes (requires minor SDK changes).

I attached the raw usage CSV and a draft SOW for option 2 for your procurement review. Can we schedule a 30-min call this week with your infra and procurement folks to walk through scenarios and cost trade-offs?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Caroline / Markus / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick reply. Per Caroline's question, attaching a concise cost scenarios spreadsheet (cost-scenario-gpu-topup.xlsx) and a short model-impact note. Quick bullets here:

Cost delta (12mo, estimated):
- +8 burst GPUs (pay-as-you-go burst): ~+$540k (variable) — best if growth continues unpredictably.
- +5 reserved GPUs (+ convert 3 burst -> reserved): ~+$390k fixed + smaller incremental burst budget — lower 12-month unit cost and better latency stability.

Model list affecting tail sequences (highest 90th–99th token lengths):
1) ClinicalSummarizer-v2 (latency-sensitive)
2) PatientQA-ensemble (ensemble calls increase tokens)
3) PolicyExtractor (long-context extractions during audits)

Recommendation: For January renewal I suggest option 2 (permanent resize + small burst buffer). Included a draft SOW (SOW-draft-Orion-v2.pdf) that maps the +5 GPUs into your dedicated pool with an onboarding checklist and rollback policy. Dev has confirmed we can perform a canary rollout and maintain existing SLAs during transition.

Next steps I propose:
- Wednesday 09:30 PT call with Orion infra + procurement to review numbers and signoff on SOW.
- Alex/Dev/Laura to prepare a one-page riser for procurement showing expected p99 improvements and cost/benefit.

Can you confirm the call window?

—Alex

Attachments: cost-scenario-gpu-topup.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB); SOW-draft-Orion-v2.pdf (PDF, 85KB)
